newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Pojistovna sees CZK 5bln in flood payments.
newsitem.headline: Czech Pojistovna sees CZK 5bln in flood payments.

text.p: Czech insurer Ceska Pojistovna a.s. said on Friday that massive flooding in the eastern Czech Republic this week could cost it around five billion crowns in claims.
"Very rough estimates calculate (the claims) at about five billion crowns," Pojistovna said in a statement released to Reuters.
The insurer, which has said it has over 100,000 clients in the flooded regions, denied reports in local media that it would have to pay out as much as 50 billion crowns.
Pojistovna said it would be able to calculate damage and its total exposure only after water levels come down.
The company said it would cover reimbursements from a combination of its reserves and re-insurance with foreign partners.

The floods forced scores of industrial companies to close down or restrict production, including car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s., tyre firm Barum Continental a.s., plastics maker Fatra a.s., iron works Zelezarnny a Dratovny Bohumin a.s., and others.
The flooding, which is reported to have claimed at least 32 lives, was moving further south on Friday while water levels were coming down on upper streams of the affected rivers.
Poland, Slovakia and Austria have also been hit by the rain-induced flooding.

Some of the thousands of evacuated people have started returning home in the north-eastern city of Ostrava and elsewhere, the news agency CTK reported on Friday, while emergency operations continued in the south-east.
